messages.subject: Milkweed
messages.text:
I have a question about your milkweed batting. Do you know if your product could be used as quilt batting and then quilted on a longarm quilting machine?

Thank you.

Sally Ciuzak

Sent from my iPad

messages.subject: Re: Milkweed
messages.text:
Hi Sally,

First off, I'm sorry for the very long silence on this. It's not the kind of service we want to give, and we're working to do better going forward.

To your question: our milkweed batting is a non-woven insulating batt, meaning the fibers are held together by a heat-bonded polyester matrix rather than being woven or needle-punched like traditional quilt batting. It quilts fine by hand or on a domestic machine, but on a longarm the tension and speed could cause the batt to shift or pull apart, especially at the edges, since it doesn't have the structural cohesion of cotton or wool batting.

That said, if you sandwich it snugly between your quilt top and backing and baste well before loading, it can work, the fibers do have a natural tendency to cling. We just haven't tested it on a longarm ourselves, so we can't promise the result.

If you do give it a try, we'd genuinely love to hear how it turns out.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
